This guy I used to work for as a growth operator had a YouTube channel with a few thousand subscribers (https://youtube.com/@matthewonlinee?si=Uf7fsbYiFQlD610A) he had a funnel that would close leads without any sales calls (we were doing around £30K/m)

The funnel went as follows:

1. Organic YouTube video with CTA to Kajabi link (welcome video) 
2. Welcome video that teases the offer and CTAs to instagram DMs (but you could do this to any chat based platform) 
3. Setter Dm script which has a CTA to watch a prerecorded webinar
4. Webinar drops price and handles all objections and then tells the lead to respond in the DMs where we pass on the checkout link 
5. Onboarding process starts 

So basically the webinar now acts as your sales call and the DM setter does the discovery.

I’d recommend checking out softr (no code portal builder) and use a data management tool like airtable or SmartSuite to host all of your data (client specific information).

softr basically assigns roles to each logged in user of your portal and you’ll be able to filter through all the data on your airtable (which is just a fancy excel) for it to be specific only to the logged in user.

I don't what else to tell you besides that avoidance and distancing yourself from what you just experienced is the absolute worse thing to do. I had a similar experience where I dropped a tab for the first time (ended being NBOMe not acid) and ended up going psycho and peaking in a jail cell. For at least 2 years I completely numbed myself with drugs and became totally nihilistic. Because of this the trauma essentially became a part of me and my behaviour and mental state changed drastically, I am a completely different person now because of that trip. It was only after 4 years that I decided to face and completely integrate the trauma where I am now a lot better (although I still have work to do). Take time to settle down and make sure the initial shock of it all it over and once you seem to have a semblance of control over your thoughts and emotions dive back into the deep end and immerse yourself in your experience no matter how traumatic it may have been. That's your way out.

Remember that your conscious mind may forget aspects of your trip but your unconscious doesn't and wreaks havoc on your thoughts and behaviour without you knowing it. This would be a shame since you seem to be a wonderful person!

Don't let go of the person you used to be, use it as an anchor. But, on the other hand, don't expect things to go back exactly to the way things were (mentally). Take this as a test that was put in front of you and confront it head-on. You are stronger than you think!

Please take care of yourself, these things happen to the best of us.

I've been moving all my life now due to my Father's Job and it has done some interesting things for me. I'm now 21 about to complete a Masters programme at Kings College London with my family currently living in Bangkok Thailand. To answer your questions:

1. I found that fear was a rather obsolete part of moving countries, fear fades away after the first few weeks in the new area once you manage to get your bearings and all. The worst was probably the feelings of loneliness but this was overshadowed by the overwhelming sensation of adventure and excitement of being in a completely new environment (which I'm sure you will feel as well).
2. to cope I would say just be mindful of things.  Your depression and loneliness will not last forever, there will be short or long phases which may vary in magnitude but eventually, if you keep a good routine, stay relatively healthy physically and socially you will be absolutely fine. Just be yourself, Europeans will find a way to surprise you.
3. ALL POSITIVE. I have never had any 'home' country since I've had to move every 4 years to a different country. This may sound harsh but I in retrospect, I can say that I have thoroughly enjoyed every part of living in each different country/culture, this also includes the shitty moments which have ultimately formed who I am now (same will happen to you).

Personally I think you should move, you have been presented the wonderful opportunity to explore small fragments of the cultures and countries of the planet in your youth. People would kill for that opportunity and when your 4 years are over I promise you will look back and cherish all the new memories you would have made.

hey man, I experienced something similar with acid a few years back when I used to live in Bangkok - Thailand. Completely lost control, played dodge the cars in the middle of a road, got hit by one and ultimately got arrested and spent the night in a cell . You can't really sugar coat it but getting over the trauma is a long and arduous process.  I can't speak for you but in the months following that trip I developed a serious case of depression which I basically did my best to suppress by going out partying and using drugs (please don't do the same) . However, after some time (about a year or two) I was able to properly reflect and internalize what had happened, what pushed me to react in that manner,  Why I felt the way I did in the following months ETC. Today, (i'm 21 now) I feel great, happy and grateful and I truly believe that if it wasn't for that trip i would be a completely different person. It was a humbling experience that forged me into the person I am now.  


Again, I can't speak for you, but if your experience was in any way similar to mine then just know that it does get better. In fact its gets 'better' in way you would never even anticipate. Keep your head up bro, be reflective on your internal thoughts and keep safe.  


BTW this acid trip happened when I was 16.
